Hand-written wrappers, loaders, and helpers in sportsdataverse.odds that are not generated API-endpoint wrappers (those have their own reference pages).

toa_event_markets(sport: 'str', event_id: 'str', regions: 'str' = 'us', bookmakers: 'Optional[str]' = None, date_format: 'Optional[str]' = 'iso', api_key: 'Optional[str]' = None, *, return_parsed: 'bool' = True, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False, **kwargs) -> 'Union[DataFrameT, Dict]' Markets available for a single event (/v4/sports/{sport}/events/{eventId}/markets). Quota: free. Parameters Returns A polars/pandas DataFrame (one row per bookmaker x available market) by default; raw JSON dict when return_parsed=False. Example from sportsdataverse.odds import toa_sports_events, toa_event_markets eid = toa_sports_events(sport="americanfootball_nfl", return_parsed=False)[0]["id"] toa_event_markets(sport="americanfootball_nfl", event_id=eid).head()

toa_usage(return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'DataFrameT' Return the cached API-key quota from the most recent call (no network/quota cost). Reads the x-requests-remaining / x-requests-used headers captured on the last sportsdataverse.odds call; all values are None until a request has been made in this session. Parameters Returns A one-row polars (or pandas) DataFrame with requests_remaining, requests_used and last_cost (credits the last call consumed). Example from sportsdataverse.odds import toa_sports, toa_usage _ = toa_sports() toa_usage()

kalshi_book_quotes(book: 'dict | pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame', *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Bid and ask ladders for both sides of a Kalshi market, asks derived from the opposite bids. Kalshi's book holds bids only. A NO bid at p is a YES offer at 1 - p, so the YES asks are the NO bids flipped (and the NO asks the YES bids flipped), with the same sizes. Parameters Returns One row per price level per side and quote, best level first (bids high to low, asks low to high): side, quote, level, price, size, cum_size. An empty book gives a zero-row frame with these columns. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.odds import kalshi_book_quotes, kalshi_orderbook book = kalshi_orderbook(ticker="KXNFLGAME-26DEC07DALSEA-SEA") quotes = kalshi_book_quotes(book) # Pipeline next step (one line) quotes.filter(level=1)

kalshi_fill_price(book: 'dict | pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame', size: 'float', *, side: 'str' = 'yes', action: 'str' = 'buy', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Average price to buy or sell size contracts against a Kalshi order book. Buying walks that side's asks from the cheapest up; selling walks its bids from the highest down. Each level fills up to its size before the next is touched. When the book runs out first, the row reports the part that fills and filled is False. Kalshi's trading fee is not included. Parameters Returns One row: side, action, size_requested, size_filled, filled, avg_price, best_price, worst_price, slippage, cost and levels_used. Prices are null when nothing fills. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.odds import kalshi_fill_price, kalshi_orderbook book = kalshi_orderbook(ticker="KXNFLGAME-26DEC07DALSEA-SEA") fill = kalshi_fill_price(book, 500, side="yes", action="buy") # Pipeline next step (one line) fill.select("avg_price", "slippage", "filled")
MarketLeague(espn_path: 'str', kalshi_series: 'str', gamma_series_id: 'str | None', draw_possible: 'bool' = False) -> None Where one league's games live on each venue. Parameters

join_espn_kalshi(espn: 'pl.DataFrame', kalshi: 'pl.DataFrame', league: 'str', *, max_date_gap_days: 'int' = 3, method: 'str' = 'multiplicative', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame' Join ESPN games to Kalshi game-winner markets, one row per ESPN game. Parameters Returns One row per ESPN game: game_id, game_date_et, away_abbreviation, home_abbreviation, kalshi_event_ticker, kalshi_scheduled_date, kalshi_away_ticker, kalshi_home_ticker, the four *_yes_bid / *_yes_ask prices (0 to 1), home_prob / away_prob (de-vigged bid/ask midpoints), prob_note (why the probabilities are null) and matched_by. A game no market matched keeps its row with null market columns. Raises Example import polars as pl from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_scoreboard from sportsdataverse.odds import join_espn_kalshi, kalshi_markets games = espn_nba_scoreboard(dates="20261122") markets = kalshi_markets(limit="1000", params={"series_ticker": "KXNBAGAME", "status": "open"}) joined = join_espn_kalshi(games, markets, "nba") # Pipeline next step (one line) joined.filter(pl.col("matched_by").is_null())

join_espn_polymarket(espn: 'pl.DataFrame', gamma_events: 'pl.DataFrame', league: 'str', *, max_start_gap_hours: 'float' = 6.0, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame' Join ESPN games to Polymarket Gamma game events, one row per ESPN game. Parameters Returns One row per ESPN game: game_id, game_date_et, away_abbreviation, home_abbreviation, gamma_event_id, gamma_slug, polymarket_us_slug (Gamma's usId as the Polymarket US gateway's market slug, aec-nba-sa-sac-2026-11-06) and matched_by. A game no event matched keeps its row with nulls. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.nfl import espn_nfl_scoreboard from sportsdataverse.odds import join_espn_polymarket, polymarket_gamma_events games = espn_nfl_scoreboard(dates="20261122") events = polymarket_gamma_events(closed="false", limit="100", params={"series_id": "12185"}) joined = join_espn_polymarket(games, events, "nfl")
